title: Agent Pulse
description: One daily evidence-backed decision brief from the coding-agent projects monitored by The Git Reporter.

scope.coverageStatement: V0.2 reports one dated decision brief from direct public source evidence and keeps git motion as a secondary measurement layer. Community feedback metrics are absent until a reproducible feedback collector ships.

inputs.dailyInsight: reported, date-owned Agent Pulse decision brief

editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — September 27, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: mastra-ai/mastra is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: mastra-ai/mastra leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 29 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: mastra-ai/mastra — 1 commit today and 1 same-day mapped article, 47.5 below its current daily pace, with 3 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
NousResearch/hermes-agent — 147 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
pydantic/pydantic-ai — No same-day commit after 190 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Check when the running agent received your correction
dailyInsight.insight: QM now records steering at native intake and places it inside the tool timeline. A sent message and a recorded intake are different states.
dailyInsight.mechanism: Harness adapters delay durable acknowledgment until their native intake path records the user entry. The web timeline splits folded work around that entry; a temporary pending chip is not a durable receipt.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: Teams diagnosing an apparently ignored instruction need to distinguish delivery delay from behavior after the instruction reached the runtime.

actions.audience: Teams evaluating the merged QM steering change
actions.label: Compare correction intake with tool order
actions.instruction: In a disposable session, send two identical corrections while work runs. Compare each recorded intake with the next tool calls and reload. Repeat with a run ending before intake; do not treat a vanished pending chip as proof of delivery.
actions.effort: One focused session per configured harness

receipts.title: Record steering at native intake
receipts.supports: Moves the recorded user entry and signal acknowledgment to harness-specific intake paths and renders it between tool activity.

confidence.basis: Merged adapters and regression tests support the event-order distinction; public validation reports live Pi/OpenCode runs and narrower Claude/Codex tests.

dailyInsight.limitation: We did not repeat live integrations or verify deployed pins. Intake does not prove obedience or undo prior tool effects. Pending browser state clears on run end or reload.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise the call if authenticated runs show intake entries appearing before the corresponding native event or live/reloaded ordering disagreeing.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Fresh authenticated Claude and Codex integration results, especially repeated identical corrections and runs that end before intake.
